title: standings() computes from matches but merges overlapping datasets and groups by raw team name
evidence: main.cpp:59 defaults competition="Brasileirao" and filters via contains() (main.cpp:52 = normalize().find()), so both the "Brasileirao" dataset (main.cpp:43) and "Brasileirao Historical" (main.cpp:47) match and are summed; the map is keyed on raw x[m.home]/x[m.away] (not normalize()), so _factual.json lists Palmeiras 902 pts AND Palmeiras-SP 622 pts as separate rows (79-row merged table; factual_accuracy=0.0). R9 criterion 'computed from matches, not hardcoded' is met, but the produced standings are factually wrong.
suggestion: Use exact competition equality (or a canonical competition enum) instead of substring contains(), and normalize team names before using them as grouping keys.

title: analyze() aggregates across ALL competitions when competition is unset
evidence: main.cpp:60 defaults comp="" so contains() is always true, mixing Brasileirao/Copa/Libertadores/Extended/Historical into one average. The requirement ('at least one aggregate statistic over the dataset') is met, but the default scope is broader than any single competition.
suggestion: Default analyze to a single competition or report per-competition breakdowns.

title: Tests are embedded as a --self-test mode rather than a separate suite
evidence: main.cpp:64-72 selftest() runs via `./server --self-test`; test_coverage=1.0 in scores.json confirms it built and passed. No skipped/disabled tests (no t.Skip/xfail equivalents in C++).
suggestion: Acceptable for a single-file C++ MCP server; a separate test target would aid CI granularity.
